sentences.text: Per: Justice Smt. Anuradha Shukla

This petition has been filed under Section 378(3) of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973 to challenge the judgment delivered on 31.12.2021 by Special Judge (Offence Against Women), Anuppur, in Sessions Trial No.96/2017 whereby he acquitted all the respondents, namely Jagdish Bhariya, Leelawati Bhariyam and Mamta Yadav, of the charges of Sections 365/109, 323 and 506 Part II of IPC.

Respondent no.1 Jagdish Bhariya was acquitted of additional charge of Section 376(2)(n), alternatively Section 376D of IPC, while respondents no.2 Leelawati Bhariyam and no.3 Mamta Yadav were acquitted of additional charges of Section 376(2)(n)/109, alternatively Section 376D/109, and 344 of IPC.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 respondent Jagdish Bhariya was the relative of Rohit, who too sexually abused the prosecutrix; the third respondent Leelawati Bhariyam was the wife of Rohit; after the expiry of 15 days, Rohit rented a room and kept the prosecutrix there for almost three months; here also, she was repeatedly raped by Rohit and respondent Jagdish.

Upon knowing the whereabouts of prosecutrix, her parents arrived and took her back to their house; during this long stay, prosecutrix was being abused and harassed by respondent no.2 Leelawati; prosecutrix tried to lodge a report but it was registered only in the year 2017 after approaching the senior police officers; Crime No.98/2017 was registered in Police Station, Kotwali, district Anuppur, against all the three respondents and also against Rohit.
After investigation, the charge-sheet was filed and the trial followed in which all the respondents and Rohit were acquitted of all the charges.

3. Assailing the judgment of acquittal in this petition, the grounds raised are that the court below committed error both on facts and in law in delivering a judgment of acquittal which is liable to be set aside as the court failed to appreciate the material evidence available on record; the evidence NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:56458 3 MCRC-20175-2022 given by prosecutrix was duly corroborated by medical evidence of Dr. Khes (P.W.5) and Dr. B. K. Prajapati (P.W.7); the reliable testimony of these witnesses was ignored and an erroneous conclusion was arrived at by the trial court.
It is, therefore, requested that the leave to appeal should be granted against the impugned judgment.
4. We have heard and considered the arguments submitted on behalf of learned counsel for the State and have also gone through the record of trial court.
5. The written report made by the prosecutrix in this case is Ex.P-4 and on its basis the FIR of Ex.P-5 was registered.

These two documents claim that prosecutrix tried to get the FIR registered at an earlier stage but her report was not lodged in police station of Manendragarh nor in GRP Station or any other police station of Anuppur helped her out but strangely written reports made to these police stations have not been produced in evidence.

If the registration of present crime was on the basis of a written complaint then it was supposed to be explained by the prosecutrix why she failed to make earlier complaints in writing and if they were in writing then why the copies thereof were not produced in evidence.
This explanation was significant in the light of the fact that the period of alleged offence was from 15.2.2016 to 10.6.2016 while the FIR was registered with a substantial delay on 1.3.2017.
The prosecutrix in this case was a major girl at the time of incident.
As per her version, she was working in some Company and still she kept silence for months together against her allegedly barbaric sexual exploitation.

Her silence in this alleged grave offence of kidnapping and gang-rape seems NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:56458 4 MCRC-20175-2022 unreasonable and unnatural.
6.
The sister (P.W.1), the father (P.W.2) and the mother (P.W.4) of prosecutrix have been examined in this case.

The prosecutrix was missing for almost four months when she was allegedly kidnapped and confined by Rohit but no missing person report was made by her family members and their statements in the Court reveal that once they met the prosecutrix, she did not narrate them the entire sequence of events which she went through.

This conduct itself creates doubt as the young prosecutrix was missing for many months, still her relatives were not making any missing person The State Of Madhya Pradesh vs Jagdish Bhariya on 8 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35804525/
2 complaint, nor were keen to know what misery she faced in recent past.

sentences.text: 7. Ex.P-27 is definitely a missing person report but it was lodged on 1.6.2017 as on that date the prosecutrix again went missing and her mother reported this fact to the police.

Admittedly,
prosecutrix gave birth to a child on 11.3.2019 and claimed that it was born out of her cohabitation with Rohit.
This fact is established by the petition filed by prosecutrix under Section 372 of the Indian Succession Act for claiming succession certificate for herself and her son after the death of Rohit.
It is admitted by the prosecutrix during her cross-examination that she claimed in this petition to be the legally wedded wife of Rohit.

8. From the facts discussed above, it is established that in March 2017 prosecutrix was claiming that she was repeatedly raped by Rohit and Jagdish almost a year back and in the month of June 2017 she again goes missing and later she claims to have delivered the child of Rohit in the month of March 2019.

These facts cumulatively reflect upon her consenting behaviour NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-JBP:56458 5 MCRC-20175-2022 for having physical relationship with Rohit and still she lodged a highly belated report against Rohit ascribing allegations of kidnapping, gang-rape,
etc.
In the light of these facts, she cannot be considered a credible witness.
It appears that with some ulterior motive she lodged the report against Rohit as well as the present respondents.
No evidence was produced to show that she was physically assaulted or abused during this period of crime.

She is a well- built lady who was living in a rented house along with Rohit and surprisingly when her relatives arrived there, she was all alone in the house, still she made no efforts to run away earlier though she claimed to have been sexually and physically tortured.

The entire scene as portrayed by prosecutrix appears to be concocted and untruthful, hence on the basis of sole testimony of prosecutrix and in the light of highly belated FIR, we find no reason to interfere in the impugned judgment.
9. This petition being devoid of any merits is, therefore, dismissed and disposed of.
10. Let a copy of this order along with the record of trial court be send back for information and necessary compliance.
(SUSHRUT ARVIND DHARMADHIKARI)
